about: Which recorded policy question an ordinance's change to a law-in-force series speaks to, and which direction counts as 'yes'. Members, voters and the record read a provision through its question (src/core2/modules/legislature.ts). A mapping, not a measurement: each row says why.

minimum-wage.question: us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.raise-minimum-wage
minimum-wage.why: Raising a local minimum wage is the policy the question asks about.

income-tax.question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-income-tax
income-tax.why: A higher local income tax shifts the burden toward earners, the side the graduated-income-tax question measures; an estimate of how members read it.

sales-tax.question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-groceries-from-sales-tax
sales-tax.why: Raising a sales tax runs against lightening sales taxes on necessities, the side the grocery-exemption question measures; an estimate of how members read it.

estate-tax.question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-income-tax
estate-tax.why: Raising the estate tax puts more of the burden on the wealthiest households, the side the graduated-income-tax question measures; an estimate of how members read it until the catalog has its own question.

inheritance-tax.question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-income-tax
inheritance-tax.why: Raising the inheritance tax puts more of the burden on the wealthiest households, the side the graduated-income-tax question measures; an estimate of how members read it until the catalog has its own question.

budget.question: us-policy-positions:fiscal.balanced-operating-budget
budget.why: More spending in a line, with no new revenue named, runs against holding the budget balanced, the side the balanced-operating-budget question measures; an estimate of how members read it.
